questions.prompt:
An airport inspection route would cross a taxi lane while a crewed airplane is approaching the
crossing on the ground. The drone is at the same height as the airplane's wing. How should the
drone crew proceed?

choices.A: Cross once the drone is above the airplane's wheels.
choices.B: Cross because right-of-way obligations begin after the airplane lifts off.
choices.C: Hold clear and delay the crossing until it can avoid interference and remain well clear.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Part 107 requires safe separation and prohibits interfering with aircraft
operations and traffic patterns at an airport. The airplane's ground movement still
presents a conflict.
A. Wing and aircraft clearance cannot be inferred from wheel height.
B. The airport interference rule also applies to surface operations.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.37 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.37
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.43 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.43

questions.prompt:
A compliant broadcast-module flight ends normally. Before a second takeoff, the module reports
a verified fault that prevents the required broadcast. A nearby monitor still shows a cached
position from the first flight. What should the remote pilot do?

choices.A: Launch and check the module only after climbing to the working altitude.
choices.B: Launch while the cached position remains visible.
choices.C: Keep the drone on the ground under the planned module pathway until the required broadcast works.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Before takeoff the module must be functioning and broadcasting the required
elements for that pathway. The cached position is old data.
A. Checking after departure does not satisfy the preflight requirement.
B. A cached position does not show that the broadcast is working now.
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.110 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89#89.110
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.115 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89#89.115

questions.prompt:
A crew has an access monitor at a temporary gate bordering the flight path. The monitor
reports a person approaching the gate just as flight control is being handed over. What
sequence minimizes exposure?

choices.A: Complete the survey line while both pilots assume the other one is responding.
choices.B: Keep the aircraft clear, confirm which pilot has control, and resume only after the gate condition is resolved.
choices.C: Have the gate monitor initiate a controller handoff without confirming who is flying.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Preserve separation, maintain a positive transfer of control, and resolve
the conflicting ground activity before resuming.
A. An ambiguous handoff delays or defeats a timely response.
C. The gate monitor's report does not transfer flight control.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.19 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.19
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt: A U.S. METAR includes the main-body wind group VRB04KT. What does that group report?

choices.A: Wind from 040 degrees at 4 kt.
choices.B: A forecast of 4-kt wind gusts from a fixed direction.
choices.C: Wind with variable direction at 4 kt.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. VRB is the variable-direction indicator and 04KT is a speed of 4 knots.
A. The group supplies no fixed direction of 040 degrees.
B. A METAR is an observation and this group does not contain a gust indicator.
Reference: FAA-H-8083-28B, Aviation Weather Handbook — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf

questions.prompt:
A private pilot submits a remote pilot certificate application using the Part 61 training
pathway and documents a current flight review. Who must verify the applicant's identity for
this pathway?

choices.A: The applicant, by attaching their own signed note of identification.
choices.B: The person accepting the submission under the rule, in a manner acceptable to the Administrator.
choices.C: The flight instructor who conducted the applicant's last flight review, regardless of who accepts the application.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The person accepting an application under § 107.63(b) must verify the
applicant's identity in a manner acceptable to the Administrator.
A. A self-attestation is not the specified verification by the accepting person.
C. A flight review endorsement supports a different requirement and does not transfer the
identity-verification duty.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.63 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.63

questions.prompt:
An unapproved practice route starts in Class G, crosses a corner of an active Class D surface
area, and returns to Class G for landing. The flight would stay at 90 ft AGL. Which part
requires prior ATC authorization under § 107.41?

choices.A: No portion, because the path spends more time outside Class D than inside it.
choices.B: The portion inside the active Class D surface area.
choices.C: Only the launch and landing points.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The authorization requirement applies to the Class D entry and segment. Time
spent elsewhere does not remove that requirement.
A. The fraction of time within controlled airspace does not determine whether authorization is
required.
C. The launch and landing are outside the Class D surface area in this scenario.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.41 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.41
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F08. Which observation best localizes the intermittent video fault
before replacing equipment?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F08 — Controlled ground-test results (fictional)
Condition                                | Original camera | Substitute camera
Original harness held flat               | Video normal    | Video normal
Original harness flexed at marked point  | Video drops     | Video drops
Substitute harness flexed the same way   | Video normal    | Video normal
Both cameras have the same nominal resolution. Power settings are unchanged.

choices.A: Both cameras have the same nominal resolution.
choices.B: The original camera works once while the harness lies flat.
choices.C: The fault appears with either camera when the original harness is flexed and disappears with the substitute harness under the same test.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Changing the harness while holding the flex test and power settings constant
changes the result. That supports inspecting and resolving the original harness or its
connectors.
A. Matching resolution does not explain why video drops only under a particular test
condition.
B. A normal result with no flex does not isolate the intermittent fault.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.15 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.15
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F02. In a classroom exercise, a planned point is exactly 150 ft
above the listed Yakima field elevation. Which pair gives the point's elevation and the
approximate length of the longest runway shown by the chart data?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F02 — Seattle Sectional - airport data (authentic FAA values, text transcription)
YAKIMA AIR TERMINAL / MCALLISTER FIELD (YKM)
Selected fields: 1099 [airport elevation field]   76 [runway length field]

choices.A: 7,750 ft MSL and 1,099 ft.
choices.B: 1,099 ft MSL and 760 ft.
choices.C: 1,249 ft MSL and 7,600 ft.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Add 150 ft to the 1,099-ft field elevation for 1,249 ft MSL. The
runway-length field gives hundreds of feet, so 76 represents about 7,600 ft.
A. The two numeric fields describe different quantities. Adding the planned height to runway
length does not produce an elevation.
B. This omits the 150-ft height and uses the wrong runway-length multiplier.

questions.prompt:
A noncertificated technician will take control to collect calibration data. The designated
remote PIC must immediately leave the control station and cannot take direct control from the
new location. Another certificated, current pilot is available at the station and can take
direct control immediately. Which arrangement allows the technician to keep manipulating the
controls?

choices.A: Have the available pilot assume remote PIC duties and directly supervise the technician before the original PIC leaves.
choices.B: Have the technician designate themself remote PIC until the original pilot returns.
choices.C: Keep the original PIC designated and ask the second pilot to take notes while the technician flies.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The noncertificated technician needs direct supervision by a qualified
remote PIC who can immediately take direct control. A coordinated transfer of PIC duties
satisfies that arrangement.
B. The technician does not have the certificate needed to assume PIC duties.
C. Keeping a PIC who cannot immediately take control fails the stated supervision condition.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.12 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.12
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.19 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.19

questions.prompt:
The proposed flight remains over a sparsely populated stretch of a river. The crew will
control it from a moving boat. Under the ordinary § 107.25 rule, which cargo arrangement would
satisfy the stated moving-water-vehicle conditions?

choices.A: The operator's own imaging sensor is carried solely for the operator's survey.
choices.B: A customer's sample is delivered under a paid freight contract, but the pilot is an unpaid volunteer.
choices.C: A customer's medicine is transported as a paid delivery for that customer.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The ordinary exception applies over a sparsely populated area and when the
operation does not transport another person's property for compensation or hire.
B. The freight is still transported for compensation even if the person at the controls is
unpaid.
C. The route meets the population condition, but paid carriage of another person's property
fails the other condition.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.25 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.25

questions.prompt:
A planned climb requires an average 450 W of battery input for 48 seconds. The planner must
keep 5 Wh in reserve after the climb. Which minimum usable energy must be available at the
start of the climb?

choices.A: 6 Wh.
choices.B: 27 Wh.
choices.C: 11 Wh.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. 48 seconds is 48/3,600 hours. At 450 W the climb uses 6 Wh. Adding 5 Wh of
reserve gives 11 Wh.
A. Six watt-hours funds the climb but omits the reserve.
B. The calculation uses hours with watts and does not produce 27 Wh.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak

questions.prompt:
A night crew member reports adequate sleep but repeatedly fails a familiar emergency
switch-identification drill under normal lighting. The drill is a required readiness check for
that role. What is the best launch decision?

choices.A: Hold launch until the crew member can safely perform the duty or is replaced with a qualified, fit person.
choices.B: Skip the check because the emergency is unlikely.
choices.C: Use the report of adequate sleep as sufficient evidence and launch.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. A demonstrated inability to perform a safety-critical response must be
resolved before relying on that person. The possible cause can be assessed separately.
B. The low probability of a contingency does not make the response capability unnecessary.
C. A report of adequate sleep does not resolve the observed readiness failure.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.17 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.17
Reference: FAA Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/training_testing/testing/acs/uas_acs.pdf

questions.prompt:
While observing a crewed aircraft on a runway approach, a student notes that the four-light
PAPI shows four red lights when viewed from the aircraft's approach path. What does this
indication mean for an aircraft on that line of sight?

choices.A: It is below the visual glidepath indicated by the PAPI.
choices.B: It is above the visual glidepath indicated by the PAPI.
choices.C: It is aligned precisely with the indicated visual glidepath.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. For a four-light PAPI, four red lights indicate a position well below the
visual glidepath. The system is referenced to the runway approach, not to drone
authorization.
B. An all-white indication is on the high side of the path.
C. Two white and two red indicate the nominal on-path indication.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/

questions.prompt:
The crew plans for the return feature to climb to a safe altitude. A configuration check shows
that the selected low-power failsafe instead lands at the aircraft's current position. The
survey route includes people outside the planned landing area. What should be done?

choices.A: Proceed because the nominal landing pad has already been inspected.
choices.B: Revise the configuration or route and verify a recovery plan that accounts for the actual low-power behavior.
choices.C: Assume the link-loss return setting controls every failsafe.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Different triggers can invoke different responses. The crew must account for
the actual landing footprint under the selected low-power failsafe.
A. Inspecting the nominal pad does not control where the low-power mode will land.
C. The scenario identifies a separate behavior for a different trigger.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.19 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.19
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt:
On a sectional, the area is on the shaded side of a blue vignette identified in the legend as
the boundary for Class E beginning at 1,200 ft AGL. For a 1,050-ft AGL position there, what
can the pilot conclude from that vignette alone?

choices.A: The position is below the stated Class E floor.
choices.B: The position is in Class E because 1,200 means feet MSL.
choices.C: The position is 150 ft inside that Class E layer.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. 1,050 ft AGL is below the given 1,200-ft AGL floor. Other overlays would
require separate review.
B. The question's legend specifies AGL, which uses local ground as the reference.
C. The difference is 150 ft below the floor.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F09. The drone has 24 Wh usable at the decision point, and the
operator requires at least 6 Wh remaining at touchdown. Which proposed plan meets that
reserve?

Action                                   | Energy used before touchdown
Finish task and return to the primary pad| 19 Wh
Recover to the alternate now             | 14 Wh

choices.A: Wait for a second pass and then recover to the alternate.
choices.B: Finish the task and return to the primary pad.
choices.C: Recover to the alternate now.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Immediate alternate recovery uses 14 Wh and leaves 10 Wh. The other plans
use 19 and 20 Wh, leaving 5 and 4 Wh, respectively.
A. This leaves only 4 Wh, below the required reserve.

questions.prompt:
A sectional airport data block reads “RP 13.” The crew wants to position a visual observer
with traffic awareness near the airport. What does the notation describe?

choices.A: A published right-hand traffic pattern for Runway 13.
choices.B: A runway heading of 013 degrees magnetic.
choices.C: A radio frequency used only by aircraft on Runway 13.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. RP plus the runway number identifies published right traffic for that
runway.
B. 13 identifies the runway in this notation rather than a three-digit heading.
C. A communications frequency is listed separately.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm

questions.prompt:
A visual observer's headset works clearly, but the assigned spot is behind a solid parapet and
the observer cannot see the aircraft in a planned sector. The pilot proposes using headset
confirmations from that spot for the entire operation. Which change addresses the problem?

choices.A: Have the observer confirm the aircraft's position from the pilot's verbal reports alone.
choices.B: Keep the position because radio contact is the only visual-observer requirement.
choices.C: Move the observer or redesign the sector so the observer can see the aircraft in the manner required by the rule.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Effective communication and the observer's ability to see the aircraft in
the required manner are separate conditions.
A. A verbal position report does not restore the observer's visual capability.
B. A working headset addresses only communication.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.33 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.33

questions.prompt:
A river fog bank occupies the low crossing but does not cover an airport on a nearby ridge.
The airport observation reports excellent visibility. What is the proper planning use of that
report?

choices.A: Assume that excellent visibility at higher elevation means the river fog will clear immediately.
choices.B: Treat it as one observation and verify conditions at the actual control station and route before flight.
choices.C: Use the airport value as a substitute for conditions beneath the ridge.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. An airport observation describes conditions at its reporting location. Local
fog and terrain can create substantial differences along a low flight route.
A. The observation does not establish the time or rate at which the river fog dissipates.
C. The ridge observation does not represent the fog bank.
Reference: FAA-H-8083-28B, Aviation Weather Handbook — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf

questions.prompt:
A motor has begun cutting out under normal power. The remote PIC has a clear recovery area
directly below the drone. The client requests one last mapping pass before landing. What is
the compliant decision?

choices.A: End the mission and safely recover using the clear area.
choices.B: Finish the pass because the preflight inspection was satisfactory.
choices.C: Continue the survey with a reduced camera frame rate.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. Continued flight is prohibited once the pilot knows or has reason to know
the aircraft is no longer in a safe operating condition. The clear area supports immediate
safe recovery.
B. A satisfactory preflight check does not excuse a later known unsafe condition.
C. A camera setting does not address the motor fault.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.15 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.15

questions.prompt:
A crew hears a traffic call of “right base Runway 09.” Which flight segment should the
observer look for?

choices.A: A segment approximately perpendicular to the final approach, before the turn onto final.
choices.B: An aircraft climbing straight out from Runway 09.
choices.C: An aircraft already aligned on final approach to Runway 09.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. Base is the leg connecting downwind to final. The “right” call identifies
the right-hand traffic pattern.
B. Straight-out departure is a different segment.
C. Final is the subsequent aligned approach leg.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/

questions.prompt:
A sensor connector was changed during maintenance. The aircraft initializes normally, but the
connector latch is not fully engaged. Which check should take priority?

choices.A: Accept the installation because the sensor was detected at startup.
choices.B: Secure the latch correctly and verify the sensor operates after the installation is corrected.
choices.C: Tape over the connector as the sole evidence that the latch is secure.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Initial electrical continuity does not show mechanical security in flight.
Correct the installation and verify function.
A. Startup detection cannot establish retention under vibration.
C. Covering the connector does not establish that its latch is properly engaged.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.15 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.15
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt:
A crew plans to hover low beside an open sidewalk where the aircraft's rotor wash repeatedly
blows sharp construction debris toward pedestrians. The nominal track never crosses above a
pedestrian. What should the crew do?

choices.A: Hold the same hover if an observer can call out whenever debris moves.
choices.B: Stop the hazardous maneuver and control the debris hazard or choose a safe flight location.
choices.C: Continue because the drone is horizontally offset from the pedestrians.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Operating carelessly or recklessly so as to endanger another's life or
property is prohibited. Horizontal offset alone does not control a known rotor-wash hazard.
A. A callout after debris moves does not control the known exposure.
C. Avoiding direct overflight does not remove the debris hazard.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.23 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.23
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt:
At a nontowered airport, a crew hears an airplane announce “departing Runway One Eight.” The
runway extends approximately north–south. Which departure direction should the drone crew
anticipate while continuing to scan?

choices.A: Generally eastbound because the digits identify a traffic sector.
choices.B: Generally southbound along the runway after liftoff.
choices.C: Generally northbound because the number is read from the departure end.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. A Runway 18 designation corresponds approximately to a magnetic direction of
180 degrees, which is south. The crew should still verify actual traffic visually.
A. The digits identify an approximate runway direction, not an east sector.
C. Northbound is associated with the reciprocal Runway 36 in this simplified scenario.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.43 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.43

questions.prompt:
Outside Alaska the official sunset is 1810 local. A drone with qualifying anti-collision
lighting will launch at 1830 and land at 1850. The briefing checklist treats this as entirely
a civil-twilight flight. What additional pilot qualification must the operator verify for this
mission?

choices.A: The remote PIC has completed the qualifying knowledge test or training required for night operations.
choices.B: No additional qualification, because compliant lighting substitutes for the night knowledge requirement.
choices.C: No additional qualification, because the takeoff occurs during civil twilight.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The stated civil-twilight period ends at 1840. The flight continues into
night, so the remote PIC must meet the night knowledge condition in § 107.29(a)(1),
including the post-April 6, 2021 test or training requirement.
B. Lighting and the night test or training condition are independent.
C. The rules apply to flight during night even when departure occurred during civil twilight.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.29 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.29

questions.prompt:
A site lies at 101° 02′ W. An approved rectangular survey area spans 100° 58′ W through 101°
04′ W and includes the site's latitude. Another point lies 5 minutes of longitude west of the
site at the same latitude. Which point lies within the longitude bounds?

choices.A: The site only.
choices.B: Both the site and the second point.
choices.C: The second point only.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The site is within the longitude interval. Adding 5 minutes west puts the
second point at 101° 07′ W, past the western boundary.
B. The second point is 3 minutes west of the western edge.
C. The first point is inside the interval, whereas the second is outside.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm

questions.prompt:
A repair replaces an airframe shell. The old shell carried the external registration number,
and the new shell has a manufacturer serial number but no visible FAA registration marking.
The registration is still current. What must be done before flight?

choices.A: Leave the shell unmarked and show the registration only if asked after flight.
choices.B: Use the manufacturer's serial number as the FAA registration identifier.
choices.C: Restore the required registration identifier to the exterior in a compliant manner.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. A current registration and compliant aircraft marking are separate
requirements. The applicable identifier must be displayed on the aircraft as required.
A. Producing registration evidence does not make the aircraft marking compliant.
B. A factory serial number is not a substitute for the assigned registration identifier in
this situation.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.13 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.13
Reference: 14 CFR § 48.205 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-48#48.205

Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F07. The crew's site rule requires both the nominal flight
footprint and the published loss-of-control footprint to avoid the occupied walkway. Which
launch plan passes this screen?

North-to-south site bands: Band 1 (open), Band 2 (occupied walkway),

Plan North | Nominal: Band 1 only | Loss of control: Bands 1 and 2
Plan South | Nominal: Band 4 only | Loss of control: Bands 3 and 4

choices.A: Plan North only.
choices.B: Plan South only.
choices.C: Both plans, because their nominal tracks clear the walkway.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The normal tracks for both plans clear the walkway, but only Plan South also
keeps the stated loss-of-control footprint clear.
A. Plan North's contingency footprint overlaps the occupied walkway.
C. Nominal clearance alone is insufficient under the stated site rule.

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F06. The stated loaded weight and moment already include the
sensor in its current mount. The same sensor can be moved to Mount Forward. What is the new
CG, and is it within the listed range?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F06 — Sensor relocation data (fictional)
Currently loaded aircraft: 16 lb total weight; 176 lb-in total moment.
Installed sensor: 2 lb. Current arm: 12 in aft of datum.
Mount Forward arm: 6 in aft of datum. Permitted loaded CG: 10.0 to 11.0 in.
The original mount is vacated. No item is added or removed.

choices.A: 11.75 in, aft of the range.
choices.B: 10.25 in, within the range.
choices.C: 11.00 in, at the aft limit with no change.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The sensor moves 6 in forward, reducing total moment by 2 × 6 = 12 lb-in
while total weight stays at 16 lb. The new CG is (176 − 12)/16 = 10.25 in.
A. This adds 12 lb-in and represents moving the sensor aft, not forward.
C. The initial CG is 11.00 in. Moving the same mass forward changes total moment even though
weight is constant.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt:
The planned landing area remains clear, but a client proposes a new escape route between two
buildings during the flight. No crew member has checked its obstacle or people exposure. What
is the best decision?

choices.A: Use the known safe recovery plan or hold in a safe position while the proposed alternative is properly assessed.
choices.B: Use the route if the live video shows the entrance is clear.
choices.C: Use the new route immediately because it is shorter on the map.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The established safe option supports recovery. An unfamiliar shortcut should
be assessed for its full route, hazards, and applicable limits before use.
B. A clear entrance does not establish conditions along the complete route.
C. A shorter distance does not establish route safety.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.19 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.19
Reference: FAA Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/training_testing/testing/acs/uas_acs.pdf

questions.prompt:
A sunny coastal site has water cooler than the adjacent land. A weak regional pressure
gradient allows the daytime local circulation to develop. Which near-surface shift should a
crew consider as the land warms?

choices.A: An onshore breeze from the cooler water toward the warmer land.
choices.B: A guaranteed lull because local temperature differences cancel wind at the coast.
choices.C: An offshore breeze caused by the warmer land being denser than the air over the water.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. Differential heating can drive a daytime sea breeze with surface flow from
the cooler water toward warmer land.
B. Temperature contrasts can drive local airflow even with a weak regional gradient.
C. This reverses the usual daytime sea-breeze direction under the stated setup.
Reference: FAA-H-8083-28B, Aviation Weather Handbook — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf

questions.prompt:
A printed sectional shows a route outside the old limits of a special-use area. A current
official notice states that the applicable lateral boundary has temporarily moved and includes
the route during the operation. Which basis should the remote PIC use?

choices.A: Split the difference between the charted and temporary boundaries.
choices.B: Use the old chart geometry until the next chart edition is printed.
choices.C: Assess the route using the current notice and applicable effective limits.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Preflight assessment uses current applicable information, including the
effective official notice.
A. Averaging the positions has no legal or operational basis.
B. A printed depiction can be superseded for the stated period.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm
Reference: FAA NOTAM Search — https://notams.aim.faa.gov/notamSearch/

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F05. At 1555Z, the crew's weather screen requires at least 3
statute miles of reported visibility and a ceiling at or above 1,000 ft AGL. Use the latest
supplied observation. What fails the screen?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F05 — Two airport weather observations (fictional)
METAR KZZZ 071530Z 08006KT 5SM BR SCT010 BKN018 10/08 A3004
SPECI KZZZ 071552Z 08006KT 2SM BR BKN008 OVC015 09/08 A3004
All times are UTC. Use the conditions from the applicable observation.

choices.A: Only ceiling.
choices.B: Only visibility.
choices.C: Both visibility and ceiling.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The 1552Z SPECI is newer. It reports 2 SM visibility and a broken ceiling at
800 ft AGL. Both values fail the stated screen.
A. The SPECI also lowers visibility below 3 SM.
B. The SPECI also lowers the ceiling below 1,000 ft AGL.
Reference: FAA-H-8083-28B, Aviation Weather Handbook — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf

questions.prompt:
A site is in Class G beneath an active military operations area whose published floor is 3,000
ft AGL. The operation remains below 300 ft AGL. What does the MOA designation establish for
this plan?

choices.A: The MOA guarantees separation for all traffic beneath it.
choices.B: The planned segment is below the MOA's published floor, while ordinary traffic awareness and right-of-way duties still apply.
choices.C: The active MOA necessarily extends to the surface below the charted floor.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The published floor defines the lower vertical limit of the designated MOA.
It is not an assurance that no aircraft will be present below it.
A. The airspace designation does not provide guaranteed separation beneath the MOA.
C. The charted floor does not move to the surface solely because the MOA is active.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm

questions.prompt:
A crew member scheduled to release and recover a hand-launched aircraft reports new double
vision that interferes with judging distance. They will neither manipulate the flight controls
nor serve as visual observer. Which decision follows?

choices.A: Keep the person assigned because the fitness requirement only covers control manipulators.
choices.B: Keep the person assigned if the customer agrees to accept the risk.
choices.C: Assign the release and recovery duties to someone who can perform them safely.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Section 107.17 applies to direct participants as well as flight-control
manipulators, remote PICs, and visual observers.
A. The person will directly participate even without handling the controller.
B. Customer approval does not remove the operating restriction.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.17 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.17

questions.prompt:
A replacement observer joins before launch after the crew has completed its briefing. They
know the radio channel but have never worked at the site. What should the remote PIC ensure
before flight?

choices.A: The replacement is informed about relevant operating conditions, emergency and contingency procedures, roles, and hazards.
choices.B: The replacement can discover those details during the first flight leg.
choices.C: Only the departure time is passed on, because the rest of the crew was briefed.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The preflight duty includes informing the persons directly participating
about applicable operating conditions, procedures, responsibilities, and hazards.
B. Waiting until flight leaves a required preparation step incomplete.
C. The briefing of others does not inform the replacement.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.49 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.49

questions.prompt:
An eligible Category 2 aircraft remains in its declared configuration, but a repair removed
its Category 2 label. A replacement must be applied before an operation relying on that
category. Which replacement meets the stated label conditions?

choices.A: A permanent label saying “Overflight approved” without identifying the category.
choices.B: A prominent, legible, English Category 2 label permanently affixed to the aircraft.
choices.C: A removable Category 2 note kept inside the pilot's transport case.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The remote pilot can label an eligible aircraft for its authorized category
if the replacement identifies that category and meets the applicable language, legibility,
prominence, and attachment conditions.
A. A generic claim does not identify the correct category.
C. A note in the case does not label the aircraft.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.115 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.115
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.120 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.120
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.135 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.135

questions.prompt:
The applicant behind an accepted Category 3 declaration finds that a newly shipped batch
contains a safety defect. The affected batch has already reached operators. What must the
applicant's product-support process be able to do?

choices.A: Notify only its own production staff until an operator files a report.
choices.B: Notify only retailers because the applicant no longer owns the affected aircraft.
choices.C: Notify both the public and the FAA of the identified condition in accordance with the rule.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The declaration applicant must maintain a process to notify the public and
the FAA of the conditions and defects described in the rule.
A. Internal notification alone does not reach the required parties.
B. Retailer notification alone is not equivalent to notice to the public and the FAA.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.130 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.130

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F03. The mission is at 1720Z. The crew plans 90 ft AGL in each
sector of the depicted route. It will use whichever authorization is valid for the segment.
Which sector needs a revision to fly the whole route as planned?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F03 — Mission route and approved ceilings (fictional)
Route: Sector A -> Sector B -> Sector C.
Authorization | UTC validity | A maximum | B maximum | C maximum
West          | 1700-1730Z   | 100 ft AGL |  80 ft AGL | Not covered
East          | 1710-1750Z   | Not covered| 140 ft AGL |  80 ft AGL
Assume both are independently valid and there are no other limiting conditions.

choices.A: Sector B only.
choices.B: Sectors A and C.
choices.C: Sector C only.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. At 1720Z both authorizations are active. Sector A is covered to 100 ft by
West, B is covered to 140 ft by East, and C is covered only to 80 ft by East.
A. Sector B has coverage to 140 ft through East even though West allows only 80 ft there.
B. Sector A is covered to 100 ft through West. Only C falls below the proposed 90 ft.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.41 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.41
Reference: FAA UAS Facility Maps — https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/uas_facility_maps

questions.prompt:
A remote PIC has ordered the first aircraft to land, but it will hover above its pad for 20
seconds before touchdown. A client asks the same person to start acting as visual observer on
a separate flight immediately. When can the person take the new role?

choices.A: Immediately, because observing and acting as remote PIC are different roles.
choices.B: After their participation in the first operation has ended.
choices.C: As soon as the landing command is sent.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The rule prevents simultaneous participation in the covered roles across
more than one operation. Sending a landing command does not end the first operation.
A. Changing the type of role does not make overlapping participation permissible.
C. The first aircraft remains airborne with that person still acting as PIC.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.35 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.35

questions.prompt:
The pilot briefs a contingency altitude of 160 ft AGL. A crew member reads back “one six zero
meters” during final checks. What should happen before launch?

choices.A: Accept the call because the number matches.
choices.B: Stop the check, restate the unit explicitly, and obtain a corrected readback.
choices.C: Wait until the contingency occurs to determine which unit everyone intended.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The readback exposed a unit mismatch. Correcting and confirming the unit
before launch prevents incompatible contingency execution.
A. The same number in different units represents a different altitude.
C. Delaying the correction leaves an unresolved misunderstanding during flight.
Reference: FAA Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/training_testing/testing/acs/uas_acs.pdf
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.19 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.19

questions.prompt:
An approved Part 107 waiver explicitly limits an operation to one named test site. A second
site has identical terrain and equipment, but it is not within the approved terms. How should
the operator proceed if the second flight requires the same relief?

choices.A: Use the existing waiver because the technical controls are the same.
choices.B: Change the site name on the internal copy of the waiver and proceed.
choices.C: Obtain applicable FAA relief for the second site before relying on a deviation there.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The holder must operate within the granted terms. Equivalent site conditions
do not expand the written scope.
A. Technical similarity is not authorization for an additional site.
B. An internal edit does not amend an FAA authorization.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.200 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.200
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.205 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.205

questions.prompt:
A Category 4 operator has assumed the applicable maintenance responsibilities by agreement.
The records are properly stored by a third-party service. An authorized FAA representative
requests to inspect them, and the service offers only an assurance that the records exist.
What should the operator arrange?

choices.A: Give the service assurance instead of arranging access.
choices.B: Make the required records available for inspection.
choices.C: Defer access until the aircraft is sold, because the records are held by a third party.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The responsible owner or operator must make the required records available
to the authorized FAA representative upon request.
A. An assurance does not permit inspection of the underlying records.
C. Storage by a third party does not defer the duty.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.140 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.140

questions.prompt:
A Category 4 operator reads an approved limitation that permits overflight of occupied moving
vehicles only while a specified automatic recovery system is available. Maintenance has
disabled that system. The crew proposes a single brief crossing. Which result follows from the
stated condition?

choices.A: The operator must restore the required system or keep the aircraft clear of the occupied moving vehicles.
choices.B: The operator can substitute a visual observer for the required system without amending the approved conditions.
choices.C: A single crossing allows the Category 4 operator to disregard the approved condition.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The Category 4 pathway requires operation under approved limitations that do
not prohibit the proposed operation. With the specified system unavailable, the condition
for this operation is unsatisfied.
B. An observer is not an approved substitute in the facts given.
C. Brevity does not override the Category 4 operating limitation.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.145 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.145
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.140 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.140

questions.prompt:
A certificated remote pilot is visiting the site to watch a demo. The visitor has no
operational task, no protective cover, and no role in the crew. The demonstration is planned
directly overhead, with no applicable category or waiver. How should the visitor be treated?

choices.A: As a direct participant because the pilot mentioned the flight in a welcome speech.
choices.B: As a nonparticipant when applying the over-people rule.
choices.C: As a direct participant because the visitor holds a remote pilot certificate.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Direct participation depends on the person's actual role in this operation.
The visitor's credentials do not make them part of the crew.
A. Receiving an announcement does not assign an operational role.
C. A certificate establishes qualifications, not participation in a particular flight.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.39 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.39

questions.prompt:
An applicant waiting to take an FAA knowledge test intentionally gives a copied test question
to another applicant before either person enters the exam room. Which conclusion follows under
§ 107.69?

choices.A: The prohibition applies to sharing a copied question with another applicant even before the test session starts.
choices.B: The applicants may share the copy because neither test session is underway.
choices.C: Sharing is prohibited only for the person who originally copied the question.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. An applicant is prohibited from giving another applicant any part or copy of
a knowledge test. That specific prohibition is independent of whether the test is underway.
B. The test-period language in the rule applies to separate provisions and does not limit the
ban on giving a copy to another applicant.
C. The rule covers giving another applicant a copy, regardless of which person originally made
it.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.69 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.69

questions.prompt:
A flight battery passes a total-voltage check, but one cell drops below the manufacturer's
minimum during a repeatable ground load test. Which decision is justified?

choices.A: Use the pack because its total voltage passed.
choices.B: Remove the pack from flight service pending assessment under the manufacturer's instructions.
choices.C: Fly the pack only on the first mission of the morning.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. A satisfactory pack total can mask a cell-level failure. The repeated
below-limit cell means safe use has not been demonstrated.
A. A total-voltage check does not establish each cell's condition under load.
C. The time of day does not resolve the cell fault.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.15 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.15
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak

questions.prompt:
During a stressful briefing, a crew member begins breathing rapidly and reports tingling and
lightheadedness. Which response is appropriate for the flight operation?

choices.A: Ask the person to increase breathing rate to sharpen concentration.
choices.B: Continue the briefing and immediately put the crew member on the controls.
choices.C: Pause the operation and have the crew member step away from flight duties until safely assessed and fit.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The symptoms can occur with hyperventilation and may have other causes. The
crew should treat the impairment as a safety concern and pause the assignment.
A. Faster breathing can worsen hyperventilation-related symptoms.
B. An impaired person should not take a safety-critical role.
Reference: FAA Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/training_testing/testing/acs/uas_acs.pdf

questions.prompt:
A civil aircraft would weigh 55.2 lb at takeoff with all required equipment and expendable
material aboard. Its mass would fall below 55 lb immediately after a planned discharge. Which
weight determines whether the aircraft meets the Part 107 small-aircraft definition for this
launch?

choices.A: The average weight between takeoff and landing.
choices.B: 55.2 lb at takeoff, so it does not meet the definition for this launch.
choices.C: Its weight immediately after the discharge, because the material is expendable.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The definition applies at takeoff, includes everything aboard or attached,
and requires a weight below 55 lb.
A. Part 107 uses takeoff weight rather than an average.
C. The material is aboard at takeoff and counts even if it leaves the aircraft later.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.3 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.3
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.11 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.11

questions.prompt:
A crew must maintain visual contact during a night operation. A nearby work lamp shines into
the observer's eyes and degrades the observer's ability to track the aircraft. The lamp can be
safely shielded without reducing required aircraft lighting. What is the appropriate response?

choices.A: Reduce the aircraft's anti-collision light because the ground lamp is bright.
choices.B: Look directly into the lamp to make dark adaptation occur more quickly.
choices.C: Control the glare or relocate to restore reliable observation before relying on that position.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Reducing glare at the source or moving the observer can restore useful
visual conditions. The aircraft's required lighting is a separate matter.
A. Adjusting the aircraft's light does not remove the ground light shining into the observer's
eyes.
B. Looking into a bright light degrades rather than improves night sensitivity.
Reference: FAA Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/training_testing/testing/acs/uas_acs.pdf
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.31 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.31

questions.prompt:
A route revision shifts a leg from a restricted area into a separately designated prohibited
area. The crew has permission for the original restricted-area leg only. What must be
addressed before using the revised leg?

choices.A: Carry the restricted-area permission forward because the two areas share a boundary.
choices.B: Avoid the prohibited area unless authorization applicable to that area is obtained.
choices.C: Assume prohibited areas are open whenever the nearest restricted area is inactive.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Permission is specific to the area and applicable restrictions. The revised
leg requires its own legal basis or must be kept clear.
A. Adjacent special-use areas do not share permissions automatically.
C. A nearby restricted area's activity status does not determine access to a prohibited area.
Reference: 14 CFR § 73.13 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-E/part-73#73.13
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/

questions.prompt:
Two compliant aircraft launch from the same pad. The first uses Standard Remote ID. The second
uses a broadcast module. Both move uphill while the control station stays at the original pad.
Which additional altitude element in the module pathway remains tied to that original launch
point?

choices.A: The geometric altitude of the takeoff location.
choices.B: The geometric altitude of the control station, labeled as a module control-station field.
choices.C: The instantaneous height of the aircraft above the terrain directly below it.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The module message includes geometric altitude of the takeoff location, in
addition to aircraft geometric altitude. Standard Remote ID has a separate control-station
altitude element.
B. The module's stated reference element is the takeoff location. It is not a control-station
field even when the two positions coincide.
C. The instantaneous aircraft height above local ground is not the geometric altitude of the
takeoff location.
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.110 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89#89.110
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.305 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89#89.305
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.315 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89#89.315

questions.prompt:
A collision causes no injury. An invoice lists $680 to restore a client's sign to its prior
condition and $420 to repair the drone. The client agrees to pay for both repairs. Which
amount and action follow under § 107.9?

choices.A: Use $420 as the relevant repair cost and omit the report.
choices.B: Use $1,100 as the relevant repair cost and report within 10 calendar days.
choices.C: Use $680 as the relevant repair cost and report within 10 calendar days.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The damaged sign is other property and its $680 repair cost exceeds $500.
Aircraft damage is excluded and the payer is immaterial.
A. The $420 charge is for the drone and does not eliminate the qualifying damage to the sign.
B. This adds the cost of repairing the small unmanned aircraft, which is excluded.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.9 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.9

questions.prompt:
An observer can see the aircraft and assess direction and hazards with ordinary prescription
glasses. With the glasses removed, the observer can do so only by tracking the aircraft
continuously through a spotting scope. Which arrangement meets the stated unaided-vision
condition?

choices.A: Use the spotting scope as the only means of maintaining the required view.
choices.B: Use a zoomed live-video feed as the only means of maintaining the required view.
choices.C: Use the prescription glasses and maintain the required visual information without the scope.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Part 107 permits corrective lenses for the required view. A spotting scope
used as the only means does not provide the required unaided view.
A. Optical magnification is not the corrective-lenses exception.
B. A video feed does not replace the required ability to see the actual aircraft.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.31 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.31

questions.prompt:
On the sectional, two depicted airports share similar blue airport symbols. One lies inside a
charted dashed blue surface boundary, and the other has no dashed blue boundary at its site.
What determines the extent of any Class D surface area?

choices.A: The applicable airspace boundary and its published designation, checked with current data.
choices.B: A universal radius derived from the blue airport symbol.
choices.C: The length of the airport symbol's runway bar.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The symbol and its color describe airport characteristics. The Class D
extent comes from its actual airspace boundary and applicable designation.
B. The symbol does not assign a standard radius.
C. The graphical runway feature does not establish an airspace boundary.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, VFR chart symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/index.cfm

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F04. At 1620Z the crew will transit Zone East at 220 ft AGL for a
nonemergency survey. It holds an authorization under Notice Alpha. Which conclusion follows
from the two notices?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F04 — Overlapping official-notice exercise (fictional)
Notice Alpha | Zone East + Zone West | SFC-400 ft AGL | 1600-1700Z
Exception: holders of individual written authorization under Notice Alpha.
Notice Beta  | Zone East only        | SFC-300 ft AGL | 1610-1640Z
Exception: authorized emergency response only. Alpha permissions do not extend to Beta.

choices.A: Notice Beta still bars the stated transit.
choices.B: Both notices are inactive at 1620Z.
choices.C: The authorization under Alpha also covers Beta.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The flight is in Beta's stated area, altitude and time. The Alpha
authorization is expressly limited to Alpha, and the operation is not emergency response.
B. Both notices are active at 1620Z.
C. The exception specified for Alpha does not extend to the independent Beta notice.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.47 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.47
Reference: FAA NOTAM Search — https://notams.aim.faa.gov/notamSearch/

questions.prompt:
Compass warnings recur on a steel platform and disappear when the drone is moved to a
previously verified nonmetallic staging area. What response best addresses the evidence?

choices.A: Ignore the warning because the aircraft is stationary.
choices.B: Calibrate on the steel platform and assume the local distortion is gone.
choices.C: Use a suitable launch point away from the interference after verifying normal behavior and a safe plan.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The repeatable location dependence indicates a possible local magnetic
influence. Choose a suitable location and verify normal indications and safe operation.
A. A stationary aircraft can still experience magnetic interference.
B. Calibrating amid local distortion can leave the aircraft with unreliable heading behavior.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.15 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.15
Reference: FAA Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/training_testing/testing/acs/uas_acs.pdf

questions.prompt:
An aircraft weighs 8.1 oz with its installed battery and propeller guards. A light required
for the proposed operation weighs 0.4 oz. Use 16 oz per pound. Considering weight only, what
is the heaviest additional payload the aircraft can carry while meeting the Category 1 limit?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. The limit is 0.55 lb, or 8.8 oz. With the 0.4-oz light installed the
aircraft weighs 8.5 oz, leaving 0.3 oz.
A. The 0.4-oz light is already installed. Another 0.4 oz would bring the total to 8.9 oz.
C. This is the difference from 8.1 oz and omits the required light.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.110 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.110

questions.prompt:
An applicant fails the initial UAG knowledge test on June 3. The testing center offers June
16, June 17, and June 18. Which is the earliest of those dates that meets the 14-calendar-day
waiting period?

choices.A: June 17.
choices.B: June 18.
choices.C: June 16.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. June 17 is 14 calendar days after June 3, so it is the earliest eligible
date among those offered, assuming other retest requirements are met.
B. June 18 is eligible but is a day later than the earliest offered eligible date.
C. June 16 is only 13 calendar days after June 3.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.71 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.71
Reference: PSI UAG Applicant Information Bulletin, p. 4 — https://media.psiexams.com/faa/UAG_Information_Bulletin.pdf#page=4

questions.prompt:
A crew discovers before takeoff that the only programmed return route would enter Class C
without authorization if a predictable communications drop occurs. The pilot suggests using
emergency deviation authority as the standing plan. What addresses the issue before departure?

choices.A: Treat an internal risk waiver as a standing FAA airspace authorization.
choices.B: Launch with the existing plan and prelabel any expected boundary crossing an emergency.
choices.C: Replan the recovery path to stay clear or obtain the applicable authorization before using it.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. Emergency deviation authority is for a qualifying in-flight emergency
requiring immediate action. A known planning gap must be addressed before flight.
A. An internal document does not supply the FAA or ATC authority.
B. An expected routine event cannot be preapproved by labeling it an emergency.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.21 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.21
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.41 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.41

questions.prompt:
A drone's airspeed is 82 kt along its track. The tailwind component along that track is 7 kt.
An alternate track would have the same airspeed and a 3-kt tailwind. With no waiver, which
track meets the ordinary Part 107 groundspeed limit?

choices.A: The alternate track only.
choices.B: Neither track, because any tailwind above 1 kt prevents compliance.
choices.C: Both tracks, because the airspeed is below 87 kt.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The tracks yield 89 kt and 85 kt groundspeed, respectively. The ordinary
limit is 87 kt groundspeed.
B. The amount of tailwind must be combined with airspeed; 3 kt still results in 85 kt here.
C. The rule is based on groundspeed, which differs from airspeed in wind.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.51 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.51

questions.prompt:
Refer to Exhibit FAA107-T20-F01. Compare the proposed 4,800-ft MSL profile to the charted
obstacle tops at the two obstacle locations. Which comparison is correct?

EXHIBIT FAA107-T20-F01 — Seattle Sectional - obstacle data (authentic FAA values, text transcription)
Obstacle 1: 4859 (499)
Obstacle 2: 2945 (316)
Compare only the two listed obstacle tops. This is a chart-reading exercise.

choices.A: The profile is 59 ft above Obstacle 1 and 1,855 ft below Obstacle 2.
choices.B: The profile is 59 ft below Obstacle 1 and 1,855 ft above Obstacle 2.
choices.C: The profile is above both obstacles because 4,800 is greater than both parenthetical figures.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer B. Compare MSL with MSL. The profile is 4,800 − 4,859 = −59 ft relative to the
first top and 4,800 − 2,945 = 1,855 ft relative to the second.
A. The signs are reversed. The first top is higher than 4,800 ft MSL and the second is lower.
C. Parenthetical figures are heights above local ground. They cannot be directly compared with
a profile in MSL.

questions.prompt:
A larger airplane has just landed. The drone route would cross the airplane's recent low
approach path near the threshold in nearly calm conditions. Which adjustment best accounts for
the wake hazard?

choices.A: Keep clear of the recent approach path until the crew can safely avoid the potentially lingering wake.
choices.B: Cross directly below the prior approach path because wake vortices cannot descend.
choices.C: Cross immediately because touchdown instantly ends any wake already generated.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. Wake generated before touchdown can persist. Vortices may sink or drift, and
calm conditions do not guarantee quick dissipation.
B. Vortices can sink below the generating aircraft's path.
C. Touchdown does not instantly erase wake already generated along the approach.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.37 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.37

questions.prompt:
Current official data identify one Class E area designated as a surface area for an airport
and an adjoining Class E extension separately designated as an extension to that surface area.
The aircraft would fly only within the extension, with no other restriction or airspace
overlay. What is the effect of the extension by itself under § 107.41?

choices.A: The separate extension designation alone does not trigger that section's airport surface-area authorization requirement.
choices.B: Every Class E area that begins at the surface triggers § 107.41 in the same way.
choices.C: Because the extension is Class E, the pilot may disregard all other applicable flight restrictions.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer A. The rule covers the lateral boundaries of a Class E surface area designated
for an airport. FAA guidance distinguishes a separately designated extension from the
airport surface area.
B. A Class E floor at the surface does not alone establish that it is the surface area named
by § 107.41.
C. An airspace-classification conclusion does not waive unrelated restrictions.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.41 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.41
Reference: FAA air traffic procedures, UAS facility maps and airspace authorizations — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Order/7210.3DD_Bsc_w_Chg_1_and_2_dtd_3-21-24.pdf

questions.prompt:
A small UAS has a receive-only traffic display. It cannot transmit ADS-B Out or reply to radar
interrogations. Which statement addresses the equipment prohibitions in §§ 107.52 and 107.53?

choices.A: Turning on a receive-only display automatically activates the aircraft's transponder.
choices.B: Any display of ADS-B traffic constitutes ADS-B Out transmission.
choices.C: Passive reception alone is not the operation of an active transponder or an ADS-B Out transmitter.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer C. The stated receiver does not transmit ADS-B Out or operate a transponder.
Separate Remote ID and right-of-way duties continue to apply.
A. A receive-only device does not automatically activate hardware the scenario says it cannot
operate.
B. Displaying a signal from another aircraft does not transmit the drone's position.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.52 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.52
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.53 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107#107.53
